findings.title: Legacy saves append answers without their scoring and scheduling updates
findings.problem: Once revision > 0, the legacy-write branch replaces the incoming blob with old.blob and changes only its log. Newly accepted answers therefore lose their XP, ability updates, streak changes and miss schedules. Flashcard schedule changes are discarded entirely. A subsequent load treats the appended answers as part of the baseline, so reconciliation does not repair the missing updates. The SQL tests only inspect source text and exercise a revision-only JavaScript helper; they never test this blob transformation.
findings.failure_scenario: A student leaves the pre-deployment app open. After another tab saves using the new client, the older tab answers a new question incorrectly. Its save succeeds and appends the incorrect answer, but the stored ability remains unchanged and no next-day review is scheduled. Reloading the new app preserves this inconsistent state.
findings.fix: Do not acknowledge a log-only merge as a complete legacy save. Either reconcile all affected progress fields consistently, or reject legacy writes and require those clients to reload while preserving their pending work. Add a database integration test that executes the trigger with an actual pre-change payload and verifies log, XP, ability and schedules together.

findings.title: Failed sign-out discards the baseline needed for subsequent saves
findings.problem: finishSignOut clears acceptedBlob, loadedBaseline and the revision before calling signOut, and neither awaits nor checks its result. If sign-out fails and the session remains active, the mounted app continues with its progress bindings erased. Its next save conflicts against revision 0 and reconciles the account against an empty baseline, replaying historical answers instead of preserving their previously computed ability.
findings.failure_scenario: An account has legacy history with stored ability n=100. Sign-out returns a server/network error and leaves the user signed in. The student answers another question. Because loadedBaseline is now null, conflict recovery rebuilds ability from the available log using fallback ratings; an incomplete legacy log or previously calibrated answers produces a different theta and answer count, which are then saved over the account.
findings.fix: Retain the account bindings until sign-out succeeds or the auth gate actually unmounts the account. Await and handle sign-out errors, keep the app usable with its original baseline on failure, and test a failed sign-out followed by a successful answer save using legacy/calibrated ability history.

findings.title: New-card reconciliation carries yesterday's anonymous count into today
findings.problem: mergeFcNew calculates anonymous introductions from base.count without checking whether base.day matches the server/local day being merged. Both devices changing to a new day therefore carries an older day's count into the new ledger.
findings.failure_scenario: The shared baseline contains yesterday's legacy ledger {day: yesterday, count: 20} without ids. Today, two devices each introduce one different card and save {day: today, count: 1, ids: [...]}. Reconciliation produces today's count as 22 rather than 2. Queue rebuilds then allow no additional new cards for the rest of today.
findings.fix: Use an empty baseline ledger when base.day differs from the merged day; only carry anonymous counts and baseline ids from that same local day. Add a cross-day conflict test with an id-less legacy baseline and distinct introductions on both devices.

assessment: Release should be blocked. Two persistence paths can corrupt saved scoring/readiness state, and concurrent saves can incorrectly exhaust the daily new-card allowance. The warfarin correction is appropriate; no new clinical errors were identified in the supplied images.
